articleTitle: Machine Learning Classification Models Comparison for Crop Damage Identification
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Plants provide over eighty percent of the food consumed by humans and livestock. Its safety is threatened by diseases and pests. The main objective of the paper is to identify health status of crop state using machine learning classification models. We manage to compare eight approaches: Logistic Regression (LG), K-nearest neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multilayer perceptron (MLP), on Indian agriculture dataset. We also used the Principal component analysis (PCA) and attempted to re-apply the same models. This paper includes an overview of these previously mentioned models, comparison between them according to data used, and a conclusion about which model leads to the best performance. Tests conducted show that the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) is the best model for these data and problem for all cases then Decision Tree (DT), Logistic Regression (LR), and K-nearest neighbors (KNN). The last three models being very close in results.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of a SynRM Based Coupled FEMM-MATLAB Softwares
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Current electromechanical power converters must meet new requirements in terms of performance, reliability and cost for various applications. Our work fits into this context with the study of a structure of synchronous reluctance machine (SynRM) which seems to meet these criteria for a high torque application. It will be about a pre-sizing a prototype of SynRM according to a predefined specifications then to optimize its mass torque via the geometry of its rotor. To achieve these two objectives, we propose an analytical-numerical approach implemented in an interactive software platform based on a coupling of the finite elements software FEMM with MATLAB. The obtained results are discussed and allow us to consider the realization of a prototype.

articleTitle: The vertical stratification (mixed propagation path: land-lake) effect on the electromagnetic fileds of lightning initiated to the CN tower
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, the Finite-Difference Time-Domain method (FDTD) is used to analyze the effect of vertical stratified ground on the electromagnetic fields of lightning initiated to the Canadian National (CN) tower in Toronto, Canada. the propagation path considered is made up of ground and a lake, adopted from the actual structure around the CN tower. The land-lake interface is characterized by right angle. The electromagnetic fields are calculated above and under-ground for different scenarios. The obtained results show, for the considered distances from the interface land-lake (dl=2m), that the two electric field components above the ground surface are affected by the vertical stratification, and that under the ground the vertical stratification effect can be neglected. The azimuthal magnetic field is not affected.

articleTitle: Modeling and Prototyping of a Fully Ironless Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D calculation method of magnetic flux density in fully ironless axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) machine. The method is based on the 3D magnetic charge representation of the permanent magnet. The real geometry of the coils and Biot-Savard law are used to model the stator windings. This modeling method allows computing with very good accuracy the main electromagnetic specifications of such unconventional machines such as magnetic flux, back Electromotive Force (EMF), electromagnetic torque, and inductances. This calculation method is applied to a prototype of a single-sided Fully Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machine for validation purposes. Calculation results are in good agreement with those obtained with experimental measurements. This method appears to be very suitable to be used in systematic design process for such structures.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis between Backstepping, Sliding mode and PI control applied to Shunt Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is a comparative analysis between three well-known control techniques applied to active power filters, namely backstepping, sliding mode, and PI controls. The minimization of the current harmonics caused by non-linear loads, the compensation of the reactive power, as well as, the improvement of the performances in both dynamic and steady-state are the main parameters of comparison. To determine the reference currents, a theory of instantaneous real and imaginary power was used in this study, where three techniques (backstepping, sliding mode, and PI control) were analyzed mathematically and then simulated to find the best control. By comparing the results, I have found that the backstepping control was more satisfactory.

articleTitle: Glucose Insulin Regulation Using Backstepping Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the regulation of the glucose level in the blood by injecting a acceptable amount of insulin for a patient where his pancreas stops delivering insulin. The metabolism of Glucose Insulin is a nonlinear system where one use the backstepping concept to regulate it’s output. Simulations are conducted to demonstrate the usefulness of the developed command.

articleTitle: Controlling the performance of a solar system using an Induction Motor-Centrifugal Compressor in the Algerian Sahara
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Excessive use of fossil energy for electricity production is a polluting factor of nature, and using conventional electrical energy in remote or deserted areas is often a costly factor, but solar energy, particularly photovoltaic, is thought to be the most convenient due to the availability of a climate to produce electricity and a sufficient area for any amount of energy appropriate. We try to size and control a photovoltaic pumping and discharging natural gas system in the Sahara by using the incremental conductibility-maximum power point tracking method to run the photovoltaic generator at full power and the vector-based method to control the associated induction motor and centrifugal compressor. With these latest enhancements, we increased system efficiency.

articleTitle: Achievable capacity analysis for power domain non-orthogonal multiple access scheme
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, we study the PD-NOMA non-orthogonal power domain multiple access technique for 5th generation wireless networks. This technique provides a solution to the overhead problems of wireless networks that have emerged due to the increase in the number of users. We describe two different power allocation schemes called fixed and fair in the case of two users. We simulated the capacity of a NOMA system using two different schemes based on the total power allocated for transmission. The results of the comparison between the two power allocation schemes show that the best performance is with the fair power allocation.

articleTitle: Grasshopper Optimization of FOPID controller with fractional filter for a GMAW Process
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Gas metal arc welding (GMAW) processes are currently of great industrial importance, being used in the manufacture of the most varied components and metallic structures and in the recovery of a large number of damaged parts. In this work, a multi-objective heuristic technique namely the grasshopper optimization algorithm (MOGOA), is proposed in order to be used in a robust welding current and arc voltage control with a fractional order proportional integral-derivative (FOPID) controller with integer filter. The problem of setting the FFOPID parameters has been transformed into an optimization problem with an objective function based on time domain and solved with MOGOA. The proposed approach has been applied to a GMAW process. The performance of the newly designed FFOPID structure (GOAFFOPID) based on the proposed GOA was compared with the GA and PSO algorithms. The superiority, potential and robustness of the proposed approach were verified through nonlinear simulation study and some dynamic performance indexes.

articleTitle: Temperature Distribution in a Buried High Voltage XLPE Cable
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a thermal analysis of a 245 kV AC XLPE cable system directly buried in the soil. The numerical computations of the cable temperature were performed using finite element method under Comsol Multi-physics environment. The effect of soil thermal conductivity on the cable temperature was investigated. The obtained results showed that the high voltage cable can operate in a moist soil with a current carrying capacity of 1022 A without risking deterioration, however in a dry soil, the temperature in the cable conductor is at the limit of malfunction and any other additional increase in heat will threaten the safe operation of the cable. Moreover, the cable temperature distribution was also investigated in desert regions characterized by very high ambient temperatures coupled with sandy soils of very bad thermal conductivity. It was found that the permissible conductor temperature is largely exceeded and if the current carrying capacity is not adjusted, the cable will overheat and its dielectric materials will be subjected to thermal aging which will greatly reduce the cable service life.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy management using a particle swarm optimization for hybrid renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study investigated a stand-alone hybrid renewable energy system’s optimum energy management system. The proposed optimization method is called Particle swarm optimization and it is an evolutionary computing methodology (PSO). The proposed technique (PSO) for managing the energy system is to calculate the amount of power that the battery must generate and that is through adjusting the values PI controller gains while taking account the amount of power generated by the significant resources (in our case PV and wind).

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Based on Crystal Polymer Liquid (LCP) Textile for RFID Medical application
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In This paper, we present a new design of multi band microstrip antenna operating at ISM band for RFID medical application. The proposed antenna is designed with LCP liquid crystal polymers substrate, which resists the effect of humidity thus allowing the antenna to keep its performance stable in an underground environment. The flexible LCP characteristics for the designed microstrip antenna is $h=4\mathrm{~mm}$ thickness, 3.16 relative permittivity and 0.025 loss tangent. The dimension of the proposed antenna is $57\times 59\times 4\mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ and the conductive parts were made of copper material. The proposed structure is light, flexible and at low cost. The study parameters are affected with integrating of slot in the ground plane for miniaturized of the size of the antenna for operating at the resonance frequency of 2.4GHz and 5.8 GHz. The peak gain is 2.94dBi at 2.45GHz and 5.39dBi at 5.8GHz and radiation efficiency is 70%. The proposed antenna is simulated using CST Microwave studio Software, and results obtained are optimized and they exhibit good radiation characteristics within ISM Band.

articleTitle: Comparative study of the quality control using fractional and integer PI controller for multivariable system based on BLT method tuning
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The distillation column has an interest research for decades due to its importance in petroleum industry and due to the complexity of controlling, because of the existence of high interaction and nonlinear. In the other hand, the increasing research in the fractional domain due to the important results that gotten. It is chosen in this work to show the effect of the fractional integrator controller on the quality control for the challenging distillation column which is a multivariable system. For that, a comparative study is used between the conventional proportional integrator (PI) controller and the proportional fractional integrator one (PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>) based on the BLT method. The wood and berry distillation column process is examined. With graphical and numerical analysis is presented. The ISE, ITAE and settling time are used as a criterion of comparison with the integer control. The results show the effectiveness and the improvement in the quality control of the response because of fractional additional parameter.

articleTitle: Study and realization of a torque measurement sensor based on strain gauges dedicated to bending and torsion
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This We have chosen the most popular tool which is the strain gauge, which is the most suitable for the torsion and bending tests we performed. We have detailed the theoretical operation of torque sensors based on strain gauges as well as some difficulties related to this method of measurement. Then we analyzed the bending and torsion tests. A design of the torque sensor has been made.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution in High Voltage XLPE Cable Affected by Various Cavities
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Since it is very hard to maintain the underground cables once installed, much care should be taken to ensure the safety, long life and high quality of its components. In light of this, electric field distribution study in a 245 kV AC Cross-Linked Polyethylene cable recently made by the Algerian factory (CABEL) is carried out. Finite element method is used to study the electrical stresses, which are the main factor that affect the cable service life. The cable electric field distribution is investigated, focusing on the influence of the presence of cavities and defects. To make a deep analysis, all the cavity parameters are taken into consideration, this allows to make a comparison of the field distortion and to highlight the critical cases which can affect the cable performances. The investigation results reveal that the electric field enhancement depends on the nature, the position and the shape of the corresponding cavity. Moreover, the presence of very sharp water cavities in the interface conductor-inner semiconducting layer is the most harmful case.

articleTitle: Characterization of Composite Insulator Response Under HVDC - Insulator Impedance and Time Ratio
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Nowadays, composite insulators are widely used in high voltage lines and for electric traction systems. The present paper aims to study the behavior of composite insulators under high voltage direct current. An experimental setup has been used to study the applied voltage and leakage current wave-forms in the presence of partial discharge, and the obtained waveforms are presented and discussed. The ratio between voltage and leakage current values illustrates the dynamic behavior of composite insulator with voltage variation. To illustrate that the dynamic behavior is not limited to magnitude, an insulator time ratio is proposed consists in dividing current peak time to the voltage one. This ratio illustrates the capacitive behavior of composite insulators under overvoltages.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study Between Subspace and Matrix-Based Error Control Solutions
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Subspace codes are codes in which codewords are subspaces from a given vector space over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Their use for error correction in Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC)-based networks has been first proposed by Kötter and Kschischang. The rationale of their application in RLNC stems from the fact that information in RLNC is basically a vector space and as long as its basis is preserved, information will not be lost. Those codes share a set of similarities with rank metric codes, which are codes with codewords being $m \times n$ matrices from the space $\mathbb{F}_{q}^{m \times n}$. In this paper, we compare the two codes and we provide insights and guidelines to follow when choosing between them for error correction. Particularly, we show that when a choice is possible for a given application, it will always be a tradeoff between code cardinality and correction capability.

articleTitle: Setting and coordination of distance relays in interconnected power systems using DIgSILENT PowerFactory software
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Maintaining selectivity among protective devices in interconnected power systems is of crucial importance. Therefore, it is necessary to install distance relays on both ends of the transmission lines to ensure efficient main and backup protection of the system. In this study, the zones and tripping time settings of distance relay for phase and ground protection of interconnected power systems are set and implemented in the professional DIgSILENT PowerFactory software. The interconnected test system IEEE 9-bus test system is used to validate the proposed methodology. The obtained results have approved that the setting and coordination of distance relays ensure adequate system protection against various fault types and locations.

Author Keywords: setting and coordination of distance relays

articleTitle: Design of quad-band dipole over a quad-band Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: A quad-band dipole antenna based on LC traps is designed to resonate at 1.19, 1.57, 2.45, and 4.2 GHz, which corresponds to GPS bands, WLAN, Bluetooth, and Radio Altimeter applications. Furthermore, to enhance the antenna gain, a quad-band AMC (Artificial Magnetic Conductor) is dimensioned and placed at distance of 0.03λc (where λc is the wavelength in free space at 1.19 GHz) from the dipole antenna. The AMC presents zero reflection phase at the four frequencies band. Considerable improvement in gain performance is achieved by providing a gain of 4.87 dBi, 5.38 dBi, 3.47 dBi and 5.22 dBi for the four operating frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: PCB Integrated EMI Choke with Low Near Field Magnetic Emission
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a PCB integration method for an electromagnetic interference choke (EMIC) and investigates its near-field emission. A bifilar PCB-EMIC structure is proposed to achieve a planar choke with better performance for conducted EMI reduction and greatly reduced near-field emission. Three-dimensional finite-element (3D-FEM) models were developed and simulations were conducted to analyze and validate the proposed PCB-EMIC structure.

articleTitle: Octagonal Planar Microtransformer for MEMS
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The work presented in this paper concerns the modelling of an integrated octagonal planar microtransformer operating at high frequencies. The integrated microtransformer consists of two planar stacked spiral octagonal coils. Basing on Mohan’s method, the geometrical parameters are evaluated. The different parasitic effects created in the stacked layers are grouped perfectly in the equivalent electrical circuit. The thermal and electromagnetic effects generated in the microtransformer are illustrated, using finite elements method on COMSOL Multiphysics 5.3 software. The gap between the coils is considered as an integrated MIM capacitor created at high frequencies leads to create a microfilter with the secondary coil.

articleTitle: Correlations for estimating optimal slope of a photovoltaic system in Algeria
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Technologies of photovoltaics is currently underrated in Algeria. Energy potential maps can help the development of the use of photovoltaic energy. Using accurate models and database of solar radiation for calculating the electricity produced by a photovoltaic system, energy production was estimated in several sites in Algeria and maps of solar and photovoltaic potential was drawn. In addition, correlations were developed to calculate the potential, solar and photovoltaic, and the corresponding optimum tilt angle maximizing it.

articleTitle: Wheat Purification of Straw Residues Using an Induction Type Electrostatic Separation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, the extraction of straw residues mixed with wheat grains using an electrostatic separator is studied. The used induction-based roll-type separator is mainly composed of an energized cylinder installed above a metallic grounded conveyor. The electric force created between induced charges on straw particles and the energized cylinder causes the attraction of straw residues. Therefore, applied high voltage and the distance between the cylinder and the conveyor are the main parameters that define the electric field intensity. The combined influence of the roll speed and voltage on the separation efficiency is evaluated using the experimental design methodology. The roll voltage and distance from the grounded conveyor are the factors for which the process is optimized. Experimental modeling results show an increase in separation efficiency when increasing applied voltage and decreasing distance. For optimal values, purity of over 98% is reached starting from an initial mixture of 71% purity.

articleTitle: Optimisation of optical and electrical properties of ZnO/Au-Pd/ZnO multilayer thin films
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: For use as transparent conductive oxide, conductive multilayer thin films were created with three alternating layers of metal oxide/metal/ metal oxide. (TCO). Specifically in this work, ZnO/Au-Pd/ZnO multilayer coating system was deposited on glass substrate and characterized. ZnO films were prepared by successive deposition steps consisting of vacuum thermal evaporation of zinc oxide powder, followed by heat treatment at 450 °C. Plasma magnetron sputtering was used to deposit Au-Pd films. the same amount of Au and Pd was used. The thickness of the sputter deposited metallic interlayer (Au-Pd) was varied in order to optimize the optical and electrical properties of the stack. Morphology and microstructure were investigated by SEM and XRD. Four point probe was used to investigate electrical properties. and the transmittance values were measured using a spectrophotometer. Transmittance was measured for multilayer stacks containing Au-Pd interlayer.

articleTitle: Investigation into effect of mixed air gap eccentricity on an injected component in acquired current signal in induction motor
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The Fourier transform is the commonly used method for the diagnosis of fault signatures in induction machines by analyzing the measured signatures such as stator currents, neutral voltage, power … It provides accurate results that are directly related to the acquisition frequency and time of the captured signal. For online monitoring, we are usually dealing with window side lobes leakage phenomenon in the spectral analysis caused by the limited time signal acquisition and analysis. These lobes are widely considered as an undesirable phenomenon because they blur the frequency spectrum. However, we have shown [1] that these lobes can carry fault signatures with the advantage of reducing the computation time and making online diagnosis possible. Using this method, this paper focuses on the online diagnosis possibilities of the mixed air gap eccentricity in the induction machine. Analytical studies and experimental results are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Correlation between Structural Changes and Dielectric Behavior of UV-Aged LDPE
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) is widely employed as insulator for high and medium voltage cable, due to its excellent dielectric, mechanical and other characteristics However, like all other insulating materials, LDPE properties deteriorate after working under different service conditions. One of the most dangerous stressing factors causing a serious degradation for the LDPE insulation properties is UV radiation. In this work, the influence of UV radiation constraint on the LDPE dielectric properties is studied. In order to support this investigation, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy is also performed. The findings indicate that UV radiation influences significantly the material insulating properties.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Three Methods for Controlling Cascaded Systems in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this study, we present a DC microgrid structure made up of two cascaded DC-DC converters. When the load converter is tightly controlled, it behaves as a constant power load (CPL) and causes system instability. Three compensation methods are employed under the variation of the DC voltage source’s input voltage to overcome this problem and minimize the ripple of the current entering the CPL. The power converter is controlled using a cascaded PI controller. While three different controls, cascaded PI, sliding mode, and cascaded PI-super twisting, are used to control the load converter. The last method allows to cancel the peaks obtained by the two previous methods. Simulation tests are performed to evaluate the performance of the three control strategies.

articleTitle: Suboptimal constrained bilinear control of a class of hyperbolic PDEs applied to heat transport in solar collector parabolic troughs
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Solar energy constitutes one of the most abundant energy resources. Advanced control techniques can have an important role in the promotion of such renewable energies by improving their efficiency. In this paper, a finite-horizon optimal controller is proposed to solve the problem of tracking a prescribed temperature profile in a solar collector parabolic trough (SC). The SC is represented by a first-order hyperbolic PDE, where the control input is the pump flow rate which generates a bilinear control problem. Based on the control parameterization approach, an approximate optimal controller is designed in the infinite-dimensional framework. The gradients of the cost function are formulated analytically, based on the sensitivity method. The approximate nonlinear optimization problem is then solved numerically using sequential quadratic programming. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the designed control technique.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis investigation the reliability requirement and challenge of XPT™ Trench IGBTs for solar energy applications
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Actually, the reliability is one of the key factors for the development of the IGBTs technologies, a resolution in Trench-IGBTs world is promoted for more significant development in the future and has been one of the most powerful drivers that forced engineers to design new products, and to match the market highest efficiency demands. The main goals of this paper based on Trench IGBTs devices (Gen3,Gen4) from IXYS technologies companies available in market during the two last year’s intended for solar energy systems by studying and evaluating their characteristics under real operating conditions UIS stress conditions. This mode of operation is therefore extremely restrictive because of the very high level of energy that the component under test must then dissipate. In this study, we highlight the effect of influential parameters on their safety zone, namely avalanche voltages (overvoltage), switching losses and switching speed. This characterization as we consider the key performances will thus provide us with objective resources aimed at optimizing the performance of these new generations of trench-IGBTs.

articleTitle: Robust Sensor-less Backstepping of DFIG based on SMO in System of Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This study presents the control (sensor-less Backstepping Control) of DFIG (doubly fed induction generator) associated with the system of wind turbine, the sliding mode observer (SMO) is used the error between the estimated and measured voltages/currents to produce surfaces of the sliding mode, the observed position/speed values are pushed to converge to the sliding surfaces. Results of simulation confirmed the performance and robustness of the sensor-less backstepping control of a DFIG associated with SMO.

articleTitle: Analysis of a new sterilization device based on ozone generation by dielectric barrier discharge
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The bactericidal effects of high concentrations of airborne ozone have been tested against Escherichia coli. Unlike previous sterilization methods, ozone is produced inside the sterilization chamber itself, reaching high ozone concentrations exceeding 1000 ppm. Ozone-generating ceramic plates are placed inside the sterilization chamber and switched on for a maximum operating time of 3 minutes. After the ozone plates are turned off, heating resistors are turned on for ozone destruction for a period not exceeding 20 minutes. The experimental study was performed using Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 bacteria. A sterilization rate higher than 99.99% was obtained for this species.

articleTitle: Design of an Optimized Fractional-Order Fuzzy PID Based-SSSC Controller for Power System Oscillations Damping
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper concerns the design of a novel supplementary controller employing wide-area signals for the Static Synchronous Series Compensator (SSSC). The proposed controller based on Fractional-Order Fuzzy Proportional Integral Derivative (FOFPID) is introduced to improve the dynamic stability and to minimize inter-area Low Frequency Oscillation (LFO) during transient conditions. The generators speed deviations are used as control signal and the regulator settings are tuned by means of Grey Wolf optimizer (GWO). Then, to clarify the advantage of the FOFPID controller against the integer PID and Fuzzy PID (FPID) an examination study was realized based on a two-machine two-area power system. According to simulation results, it was demonstrated that the designed SSSC-based FOFPID controller provides better performances for damping inter-area LFO compared to PID and FPID controllers.

articleTitle: Discharge of polypropylene films surface negatively charged
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The space charge, present in dielectrics materials, such as the polypropylene films or fibrous nonwoven media, is not generally appreciated. Indeed, the local intensification of the electrical field can provide local discharges. It is necessary to eliminate these charges. The aim of this work is to propose a simple device for the elimination of electric charges and to evaluate its efficiency using non-contact measurements of surface potential. The characterization of the state of charge is obtained by the surface potential before and after charges elimination. To control the neutralization, the use of the triode configuration is a wise choice. Indeed the grid connected to the earth makes it possible to impose a zero potential on the surface of the dielectric.

articleTitle: Image segmentation for measuring growth coefficients of wheat used in precision agriculture
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Water deficit affects several physiological variables of the plant and is synonymous with a decrease in yield and quality for field crops such as wheat. Irrigation is therefore a recommended solution. Agronomic image processing has enabled the development of several tools to deal with the phenomenon, by combining sensors and models such as the percentage of soil cover PGC and crop coefficient Kc. The aim of our work is the development of an indicator of the condition of the crop plants, accessible by video surveillance using image segmentation based on the multiphase level set model, allowing the early detection and prevention of water stress. Repeated images were taken on control plants at several stages of crop development.

articleTitle: Simplified Complex Joint Diagonalization Algorithm and Source Separation of Breathing Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In the present paper, we have treated the Complex Joint Diagonalization (CJD) problem by proposing a non trivial simplified version of an efficient CJD algorithm based on generalized Givens rotation. The novelty of this approach lies in the optimization step used in order to estimate the complex phase of the generalized Givens rotation. Numerical simulations are conducted in order to compare the performance of our algorithm with the major existing solutions. The developed method has been applied to a real-life application that concerns the separation of breathing signals. These signals are obtained by continuous wave radar illuminating two seating and breathing persons. The results show us the effectiveness of the proposed method in separating the breathing signals.

articleTitle: Parameters Extraction of Photovoltaic Module Using Giza Pyramid Construction Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: in this paper, an ancient inspired algorithm called Giza Pyramid Construction (GPC) is used to extract the five unknown parameters in the one diode model of a PV module. The conducted investigation on the accuracy to extract the five parameters shows that GPC algorithm gives good convergence rate toward the global minimum. The obtained parameters from GPC approach are used to plot the predicted IV and PV curves characteristic and compared with the measured IV and PV curves. These extracted parameters are used to predict the dynamic evolution of the voltage and current at the maximum power point and the findings agree with the measured quantities.

articleTitle: Optimal sizing of photovoltaic water pumping system using Fuzzy-Adaptive PSO
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Water is engine of all human activity. This year Algeria has experienced a shortage of water supply which has made groundwater a semi-main source for reserve. Photovoltaic-based water pumping system (PVPS) presents an attractive solution to water access, especially in irrigation needs. In this regard, the main objective of this article is study investigates an optimization approach of photovoltaic energy for pumping systems based on technical and economical indicators. In order to ensure the best size of system elements, The algorithm optimization is configurated using fuzzy–adaptive particle swarm optimization (PSO). The recommended model takes into account initial capital cost, operation, and replacements costs. The simulation analysis is mainly affected by load, meteorological data elements parameters. For this study, an autonomous PVPS is designed to satisfy meet water demand for irrigation of small agricultural field over 20 years life span in Algiers. The results include optimal numbers of each component including pumps and batteries for storage supplied by photovoltaic panels taken as renewable energy sources which provide photovoltaic pumping systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Receiver for MCM Based NOMA in Doubly Selective Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has been identified as a potential fundamental shift for the design of multiple access systems. Over a high Doubly Selective (DS) channel scenario, this paper considers the use of NOMA system based on Multi-Carrier Modulation (MCM) with various waveforms, with Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Filter Bank Multicarrier Modulation (FBMC) as special cases. Furthermore, we investigate the Imperfect Successive Interference Cancellation (I-SIC). NOMA users are affected by intra-user interference and inter-user interference in this situation. To this end, an adaptive receiver scheme that combines one-tap equalization and a joint iterative interference cancellation, proposed in literature, is introduced. The receiver selects the appropriate data detection mechanism based on the power allocation factor and hence the channel constraints. The One-Tap equalizer is so useful in practice. Unfortunately, once the DS channel and NOMA induced interference begin to dominate the noise, a one-tap equalization under-performs. On the other hand, by using the joint iterative interference cancellation approach, performance will be greatly improved at the cost of computational complexity. Moreover, numerical simulations are carried out to illustrate the efficacy of the suggested combined strategy in contrast to the theoretical Perfect-SIC (PSIC) condition.

articleTitle: Performances Improvement of PV Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This research discusses how an exemplary operation of a solar pumping system based on a Permanent magnet brushless direct current (PMBLDC) motor driving a centrifugal pump might be attained. The optimization task consists in optimizing the efficiency and the daily pumped water quantity. Furthermore, a comparison is conducted between the direct coupling (DC) of the system (without optimization), the optimization using the conventional technique (CM), and lastly, the optimization with the genetic algorithms (GA). The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach of genetic algorithms for the enhancement of efficiency and the maximum quantity of water pumped.

articleTitle: Wavelet leader-based multifractal analysis for characterizing subsurface heterogeneities using velocity logs
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In petroleum engineering, well logs are the key to characterize a hydrocarbon reservoir, and to extract meaningful features related to the lithology and the type of fluids present in the reservoir. Several approaches have been suggested to exploit well log data. In this view, this paper presents a wavelet leader-based multifractal analysis (WL), applied to velocity log data measured at two scientific deep boreholes: the pilot well (KTB-VB) and the ultra-deep main well (KTB-HB), to study the local behavior and the invariant scale properties of the investigated data. The suggested approach allows distinguishing different lithology types based on the wavelet leaders. First, local regularity profiles have been computed using the Peltier and Lévy-Véhél (PLV) algorithm from the different velocity logs, and a lithological segmentation has been carried out. Then, a multifractal analysis has been carried out on velocity logs using the WL algorithm. A clear correlation is shown between lithology and multifractal properties extracted from the investigated logs, specifically significant values singularity spectrum width $( \Delta h)$ correspond to the local filled fractures. To conclude, the singularity spectrum may then serve as a tool for characterizing subsurface heterogeneity and identifying a zone of macro- and micro-fractures.

articleTitle: Effect of Al:F codoping on the optical ans structural properties of SnO₂ films
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The present work deals with the deposition of SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin films by a simple technique such as spin coating. In the first, a set of pure SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film and (Al/F) co-doped were prepared using various deposition conditions in order to prepare suitable films devoted to the optoelectronic and sensing applications. The aim of this work, is to study the effect of codoping on optical and structural properties of tin dioxide (SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) thin films. From the optical characterization results, we inferred that the deposited films have suitable optoelectronic properties for the photovoltaic applications since they present a good transmission in the visible range. The structural charactherization of the doped films show the beginning of crystallization with apparent peaks whose intense peak is along the diffraction plane (101).

Author Keywords: thin films-SnO₂ – spin coating – optoelectronic – sensor

articleTitle: FPGA-based Neural Network System for Epileptic Seizure Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: An epileptic seizure is the maximum replied persistent neurological disorder. The non-stop tracking and early detection can reduce the effect of seizures. In this context, we aim to realize a hardware implementation system based on a multi-layer perceptron able to detect epileptic seizure activities. The designed system has been implemented on FPGA. We have proposed an optimized medical diagnostic approach based on wavelet transform with a minimum number of features, able to correctly classify the appropriate Electroencephalogram (EEG) classes. The optimized approach leads to minimizing the size of the FPGA prototype and reducing power consumption. The proposal system performance has been realized in terms of precision rate and the number of resources used in hardware implementation.

articleTitle: A Novel UWB Printed Monopole Antenna with Enhanced Frequency Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, an ultra wideband monopole antenna with an extended frequency bandwidth has been developed. This mainly consists on introducing defects with suitable shapes and locations to an original circular antenna that resulted in a significant bandwidth enhancement. A prototype of the obtained structure has been fabricated and its reflection coefficient measured where a good agreement is noticed between simulated and experimental results. The antenna simulated bandwidth [2.150-15.253 GHz] makes it suitable for the several wireless applications operating in this frequency interval.

articleTitle: Predicting PEMFC maximum power point using an artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict the maximum power point (MPP) of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). First, the fuel cell is modeled and simulated using the Amphlett model. Then, we develop a tracking algorithm for maximum power point based on a Radial Basis Function (RBF) Artificial Neural Network (ANN) in order to calculate the maximum power point defined by its current and voltage whatever the fuel cell operating conditions (oxygen and hydrogen partial pressures, operating temperature and membrane hydration rate). The Amphlet PEMFC electrochemical model is used to generate the training examples of the proposed neural network and to validate the obtained results. The results show that the ANN can accurately predict the fuel cell current and voltage at the point of maximum power for all operating conditions.

articleTitle: Contribution to Reconfigured Rectifiers Fed Gas Metal Arc Welding Process
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The welding process is among the most important technologies used and included in the world of manufacturing, related to welding and metals, there are several machines related to welding, among the most important, the most common, and the most recent of them is a machine of Gas Metal Arc Welding, it is fed by the static converter i.e. the rectifier. This paper deals with the study of the behavior of the welding machine GMAW in healthy and faulty cases, under the faulty case; the open-circuit fault occurs at the switches in one of two rectifiers. This paper proposes the inclusion of a new method for diagnosing the faults; it adopts the threshold band technique for early detection of open-circuit faults related to Thyristor switches, it also depends on the polar coordinates technique to accurately locate the faulty switches. Therefore, this paper proposes the installation of fault-tolerant rectifiers. The results obtained in this manuscript demonstrate the efficacy of each of the proposed diagnostic methods the fault-tolerant rectifiers included, all this contributed to ensuring the smooth running of the welding process; by maintaining the work-piece on one hand and the other hand, protecting the network from current distortions caused by open-circuit faults.

articleTitle: A Novel Radiation Pattern and Frequency Reconfigurable Single-Armed Spiral Microstrip Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of a reconfigurable printed spiral antenna is presented. To achieve both pattern and frequency reconfiguration, pin diode switches are integrated within the radiating antenna surface. CST and ADS simulation softwares are used to design and analyse the antenna structure and performances. simulation results are presented and compared. The proposed antenna is able to configure operating frequencies in the frequency range of 1-6GHz and provides a beam switching in the elevation plane between −44° and +44°. Circular polarization characteristic is inspected; the axial ratio remains within an acceptable limit for the majority of the switching cases. The gain, which is approximately 8.5dB, stays relatively constant within ±0.5 dB variation.

articleTitle: Modelling of Constant Voltage Transformer for Transient and Parametric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper present a model of a Constant Voltage Transformer (CVT), with consideration for transient and parametric simulation. The interaction of the ferroresonant circuit and the geometric parameters such as windings, capacitor, and shunt reluctance on the CVT performance is studied, and the determination of the parameters for a better operation is achieved. This model is implimented with Matlab/Simulink where the behaviour of the nonlinear reluctances is modelled by a simple hysteresis model with considering of the core loss. The experimental results are compared with the simulation results under different conditions to validate the implemented model.

articleTitle: Compact Tri-Band Two-Element MIMO Slot Antenna for 5G Sub-6 GHz Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: in this paper, a compact two-element triple band, multiple-input multiple-output antenna for fifth-generation (5G) New Radio (NR) sub-6 GHz is presented and discussed. The single-element antenna consists of a $50 \Omega$ microstrip feed line where three open-ended slots are etched on the ground plane (DGS). The proposed 2-elements MIMO antenna has dimensions of $34 \times 32.5 \times 1.57$ mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A wide slot is cut off between the two ports to reduce the mutual coupling in the structure. Operating bands of the proposed MIMO structure are obtained from 2.23 to 2.50 GHz, 3.53 to 3.71 GHz and 5.46 to 5.84 GHz with relative bandwidths of 11.42 %, 4.97 % and 6.7 %, respectively. The minimum isolation for the entire frequency operating band is greater than 18 dB. Diversity performance (ECC, DG, etc.) is calculated and analyzed from the simulated and measured S-parameters. The obtained results are compared with other works published recently.

articleTitle: Cross-Current Minimization in Modular System with Unbalanced Line Impedances
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Circulating current is one of the major tasks to deal with when parallel inverter option is involved. In this paper, new modulation strategy is developed to minimize the circulating current for common DC input voltage case. These circulating currents are sensitive to line impedance values. The present work is relative to the case where different and unbalanced line impedances are linked to the common point of connection. Based on the average phase-leg technique, new sinusoidal pulse-width modulation parameters, with respect to the line impedance value of each leg, were formulated to reduce the circulating current. Experimental results were gathered to first validate that paralleling inverters lower the total harmonic distortion of the load current and second the new modulation strategy decreases respectively by more than 89% and 40% the fundamental component and the RMS value of the circulating current.

articleTitle: Simulation of electrical field and potential on multilayer superhydrophobic insulation with water drops under DC voltage
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The study of the electrical performance of an insulator in the laboratory requires a lot of time and energy. For this reason, a simulation method using COMSOL Multiphasic software has been developed to facilitate this task. This paper presents simulation results of the electric field and potential distribution of insulating with multilayers of superhydrophobic surface, with the presence of water droplets. The objective of this work is to predict the movement of expulsion of water drops outside four-layer superhydrophobic insulation, with variable permittivity degree of solid insulating cover and their effect on the distribution of the field and electric potential. In addition, a comparison between the performance of superhydrophobic single-layer insulation with that of multi-layers is carried out. The simulation results show that the intensity of the electric field on the insulation is greatly influenced by the variation in the number of water drops deposited on the superhydrophobic insulation, as well as, by the value of the relative permittivity of the cover. On the other hand, the addition of other superhydrophobic layers has a slight influence on the distribution of the electric field.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Magnetometer for Future Algerian Satellites: Evaluation of Earth Magnetic Field Modelling with Python
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The recent objectives set by the Algerian Space Agency (ASAL) concern the development of a satellite platform. In this perspective, a set of instruments for attitude control and determination shall be developed. One of these instruments is the magnetometer. In fact, satellite attitude determination from the earth magnetic field measurement is commonly used for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. The first step of this development is the subject of this paper, where the data related to the earth magnetic field affecting the satellite is simulated using open source solution based on python libraries to compare the results with the powerful software dedicated to space applications (Systems Tool Kit: STK). The obtained results show that python is capable to model the earth magnetic field with small difference compared to STK. These results will ultimately allow us to choose the appropriate technological solution that will be used for the development of our in-house Earth’s magnetic field sensor.

articleTitle: Using computer vision to assess an electrostatic separation process
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: For slow-varying processes like particles’ movement in some electrostatic separators, computer vision using a standard camera can be a simple and cost-effective tool for process assessment. This paper is aimed at using video treatment to track particle position as well as evaluate separated material purity in an inclined-plane electrostatic separator. The technique is applied to a 50%–50% binary mixture of polyamide (PA) of blue color and polycarbonate (PC) of orange color. Based on image treatment, each color can define the particle position, allowing a fast mapping of global particles’ distribution. The obtained results have allowed not only particle tracking but also estimation of the purity of recovered materials based on particle counting on both sides of the separator. The calculated purity rates are in good agreement with the measured values.

articleTitle: A Technique for Filtering Ground Clutter in Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper deals with the detection and filtering of rain cells extracted from images taken by a weather radar. The intended impact is: on one hand, to extract the correct rain rate contained by these images and on the other hand, to increase the performance of these types of remote sensing devices. This is to automatically identify cloud masses, characterize them and predict their evolution over the time. To analyze this phenomenon, we used 512 x512 pixels radar images taken in the region of Setif in eastern Algeria. Our study consists of eliminating parasite echoes resulting from the ground in particular due to the mountain surrounding the radar, by using textural parameters. For every type of echoes we calculate the parameters of Unser into a 5 $\times $ 5 pixels window by sweeping the entire image. Then we present the histograms of these parameters and determine the discrimination thresholds for each one of them. The simulations results obtained from the local homogeneity, the variance of the differences, the entropy, the entropy of the sums, the entropy of the differences, the energy, the energy of the sums and the energy of the differences are very satisfactory with a probability of difference factor greater than 95%. We have found that the most dominant textural parameters are the Energy of differences and Variance of the sum as the major part of the ground echoes have been successfully removed without altering the precipitation echoes. The reason is that for these two parameters, the probability of difference factor was over 98%, which is better that the rest of the parameters.

articleTitle: FPGA-based Algorithm for Harmonic Current Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The present paper deals with problems related to the damaging effect of nonlinear loads that expressed in harmonic current, where we proposed an instantaneous calculation of the sinus and cosine functions related to the fundamental frequency using a multi-variable filter (FMV).The main idea is to go beyond the limits caused by the use of PLL so as to extract instantaneously and precisely the fundamental component of the voltage of the power system. To do that the FMV algorithm is implemented on the FPGA and the Newton-Raphson algorithm is depicted in order to calculate the needed inverse square root where the obtained sine and cosine functions are used to optimize the instantaneous imaginary power algorithm for extracting the harmonic components. Simulations and exprimental results are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed study.

articleTitle: Speed controller efficiency of the TSR based MPPT of a variable speed wind power system
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper compares the usefulness of linear and nonlinear control laws applied in MPPT based on the TSR algorithm in the wind power system. The main idea of this paper is to show the improvement brought by the higher order sliding mode control based on Supertwisting compared to the conventional PI to mitigate the chattering phenomenon, cancellation of the hyperlink between the controller parameters and the mathematical model of the system and the reduction of the sensitivity to external disturbances. The results obtained confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control laws during all the operating modes of the variable speed wind power system in extracting the available maximum aerodynamic power.

articleTitle: Acoustic Analysis of Standard Arabic Emphatics using the LPC Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: this paper presents the conception of analysis tool whose efficiency tested in an acoustic investigation emphatic sounds of Standard Arabic (SA). During software development, techniques based on computational algorithms are used in programming, in particular the algorithms of automatic Formant extraction using Linear Prediction Coding (LPC) to develop the analysis parameters which are significant factors for acoustic structure development language. The acoustic analysis aims to measure vowel formant frequencies (F1-F3) of phonemes [d], [t], [z], [s] their non-emphatic counterparts [d], [t], [z], [s] and at initial, medial, and final position. Formant structures show the effect of emphatic consonants on SA vowels by a raised F1, lowered F2, and raised F3 in the vowel adjacent to the emphatic consonant. The pattern across a rapprochement between F1 and F2 suggests that emphasis involves a constriction near the epiglottis.

articleTitle: Solar Home Energy management based on weather forecasting
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy management strategy using weather forecasting to improve the energy consumption in grid-connected residential PV system with storage. The predicted PV production is used by a developed Home Energy Management in such a way to match the energy demand while achieving high degree of self-consumption. It has been shown that the Self Sufficiency could be improved by 14% in winter days by scheduling the sorted loads by priority.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis of surface disinfection system in hospitals using dielectric barrier discharge ozone generator
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Hospitals are important sources of pollutants that can expose public to the risk of infection through the transmission of nosocomial pathogens that are localized on contaminated surfaces Therefore, it is important to reduce the risk of contamination inside hospitals by using reliable and effective disinfection techniques. Ozone disinfection has been used and proven effective as an alternative sanitation technology to conventional disinfectants in reducing microbial contamination. In this paper, the disinfection capacity of the ozone gas is studied by analysing the reduction of bacteria colonies after ozonation on different points of an ablution room in the forensic medicine service of university hospital centre CHU of Sidi-Bel-Abbes. The objective of our work is to carry out an experimental study to determine the capacities of ozone generator disinfection with using microbiological analysis.The results obtained showed a high disinfection efficiency with rates well above 80%.

articleTitle: A comparative Study of Channel Shortening Equalizer Designs in THMA-UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presented a relative comparison of the proposed design of channel shortening equalizers (CSE) design [1] in Time-hopping multiple access ultra-wideband (THMA-UWB) systems with the classical maximum shortening SNR (MSSNR) CSE, minimum delay spread (MDS) CSE and some commonly used Rake receivers. An overall assessment depicts that the proposed CSE design outperforms the competitive CSEs and Rake structures in terms of some key performance indicators of the system. The proposed design is relatively less complex and captures more signal energy from the user of interest while maintaining better relative BER and allows the system to achieve higher data rates. A key tradeoff which is ever present in any system is the complexity versus performance. On the basis of performance analysis, we can state that using a CSE with Rake receiver combining is a better solution than MSSNR, MDS, A-Rake, S-Rake and P-Rake in terms of performance and system complexity. It enables the effective receiver with less number of fingers saving hardware cost and complexity.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of the PCB Layout effect at the switching node level of a GaN-Based Power converter
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, a critical point of the switching loop of a synchronous power converter with Gallium Nitride (GaN) switching devices is investigated. Printed Circuit Board (PCB) designs are proposed to optimize the performances of the power converter at this point level. Electromagnetic (EM) modeling approach is employed to model and characterize the switching node junction stray inductance contribution of the proposed designs. These designs yielded distinct performances in terms of low (Electromagnetic Interferences) EMI and low current stress in the hot point of the converter. The fourth design demonstrated the best compromise between the two constraints.

articleTitle: Dual Band Cup-shaped Microstrip Monopole Antenna for WLAN/WiMAX Application
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this article, a novel design of a compact dual band planar monopole antenna has been presented. The antenna radiating patch consists of a slotted cup-shaped structure operating in the two bands covering the 3.5/5.5 WiMAX and 5.2/5.8 WLAN applications. The proposed radiating patch is fed by means of 50 Ω micro strip line. For better impedance matching, an inset is inserted. The dual band operation is achieved by loading two symmetrical rectangular open slots on the a wide band radiator patch. FR-4 substrate with relative permittivity of 4.3, loss tangent of 0.017 and thickness is used to fabricate the structure. The total size of the proposed design is 26x22x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The measured return less results are found to be in good agreement with the simulated ones. Moreover, the H-plane simulated radiation patterns, at both operating bands, are omnidirectional, while bidirectional radiation patterns are obtained in the E-plane at both operating bands. Accordingly, the slotted-cup shaped proposed structure is well suited to be used in wireless applications.

articleTitle: Efficient Wideband Diode Mixer for k-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, an efficient k-band diode mixer was designed in TSMC CMOS 180 nm technology. It works in the frequency range of 17-28 GHz with a conversion loss of 7.5 dB for an IF frequency of 3 GHz and a local oscillator power of 15 dBm. It exhibits an isolation better than 30 dB between the input LO and RF ports and the IF output port. Furthermore, the proposed mixer shows low conversion loss particularly for high IF frequencies.

articleTitle: Fractionel Order PID Controller Design using Particle Swarm Optimization for an Arc Welding Machine Fed via a Bridgeless PFC Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This article presents the design of the fractional order PID controller by using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm for controlling an arc welding machine supplied via a bridgeless power factor correction converter (PFC), This welding system is able to enhance the power quality of the arc welding power supply (AWPS), in welding circuit side, the PSO algorithm is used used to determine the unknown parameters of the FOPID controller such as $K_{p}K_{i},\ K_{d},\ \lambda$ and $\mu$ by minimizing an aggregated cost function based on the integral time absolute error (ITAE) between the welding voltage $V_{\mathrm{w}}$ and its reference, this proposed controller is used to regulate the welding voltage and current. Also, in grid grid side, another control scheme uses a FO-PID controller to manage the DC-link capacitor voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</inf> of a bridgeless PFC converter. The PSO-FOPID controller have operated cooperatively with FOPID controller, like faster response to the welding load variations, which results in an improved of weld bead quality and obtained the excellent welding performance. The performance of the optimal controller is examined in MATLAB/Simulink environment. It is also compared with the performance while using other controllers such as the PI and FOPID controllers. In addition the designed controllers gives a good welding voltage regulation under different operating condition, also the AWPS has a good power quality in terms of THD and PF.

articleTitle: On the Contribution of A PV Generation in Adrar’s Isolated Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper aims to study and analyse a 220 kV isolated power plant of Adrar, Algeria. This power system is mainly composed of nine buses and seven PV power plants. Simulations are conducted using this power system where the irradiance, power demand and temperature variations are considered. Firstly, the effect of PV module temperature on the generated power is presented and discussed. Secondly, the load flow is analysed during 24 hours in order to evaluate the overall contribution of the PV generation, especially during rush hours. Finally, the transmitted power is also studied, showing the purpose of the related high voltage lines.

articleTitle: A Two-Element Slotted Cup-shaped Compact Monopole Antenna For MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: A two-port MIMO antenna array with wideband and high decoupling characteristics for wireless systems operating in the frequency range extending from 2.9 to 4GHz covering 3.5 WiMAX bands is proposed. The antenna element consists of a slotted cup shaped monopole radiating element fed with $\mathrm{a}50 \Omega$ transmission line. The high isolation between the two elements is achieved by inserting a rectangular stub in the ground plane along with etching two DGS slots. The inserted DGS slots not only improve the isolation between the antenna elements but also improve the impedance matching and widen the operating band width. Besides demonstrating a small footprint of $26 \times 44 \times 1.6$ mm3, the proposed two-port MIMO antenna array has also shown a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 26% (2.9-3.75 GHz), strong isolation of more than 22 dB, and good gain and efficiency of around 2.87 dBi and 98%, respectively, across the band of interest.

articleTitle: Surface treatment of thin films deposited by plasma PECVD prepared for an application as biocide material
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, properties of thin films deposited by plasma enhanced chemical vapor (PECVD) method have been studying. Films have been elaborated from pure HMDSO precursor and/or mixed with different proportion of oxygen gas. Contact angle measurement reveal that deposited films have a hydrophobic character for films deposited from pure Hexamethyldisiloxane (HMDSO) with contact angle value around 110°. Whereas, contact angle decrease gradually with oxygen proportion to achieve 17° for film deposited from 90% oxygen proportion, which indicated that deposited films have hydrophilic character. FTIR analyses and optical emission spectroscopy analyses has been used to investigate the physicchemical properties of deposited films.

articleTitle: Design of A New Earth Network for the 60/30 KV SI Mustapha Substation
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this work, we study the sizing of the ground network of the 60/30 kV substation for the transformation and distribution of electrical energy of Si Mustapha. The ground study provides the maximum permissible step (Ep) and contact (Ec) voltages according to IEEE Std 80-2000, as well as the evaluation of the ground surface potential GPR. The ground grid study can determine the values and produce the actual step and contact voltages profiles as well as the equipotential contours of the contact and/or surface voltages in 2D and 3D. The simulation is done by the CYMGRD software, the soil resistivity measurements, were executed by WENNER method using the CHAUVIN Arnoux C. A 6470 at selected points East, North and South of the substation.

articleTitle: Novel Propagation Characteristic Expressions of Anisotropic Rectangular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper introduces novel expressions to analytically determine the phase constant of EM fields in an homogeneous uniaxial electric and magnetic anisotropic rectangular waveguide (RWG) with arbitrary transverse dimensions, while focusing on the fundamental mode. To successfully evaluate the reliability of the proposed analytical results, the numerical modeling method of moments was used with the operator formalism concept for an easier formulation of the boundary conditions. Selected trigonometric trial functions lead to more accurate analysis of such RWG since close agreement was found between the results obtained from our analytical expressions and those given by the numerical method.

articleTitle: Comparison between the theoretical and experimental Effectiveness in the Rod-barrier-plane System
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The present paper deals with the influence of insulating barriers on the breakdown and the effectiveness in the Rod-insulating barrier-plane air gap system under AC voltage. The influence of different parameters, such as gap distance between electrodes and barrier dimensions, is studied. Every value is the average of five experimental tests. The results showed that the rigidity increases with the width and decreases with the gap distance, the thickness has an effect on the effectiveness variation, it increases with thickness. A theorical model, using electric field distribution obtained by finite element method, to estimate the effectiveness is established. It was verified that the established model reproduces correctly the experimental results.

articleTitle: Physical, electrical and dielectric properties of pure ZnO thin films deposited by SP method: Effect of substrate temperature
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: The aim of this study concern in the optimization of the physical and dielectric properties of pure ZnO thin films deposited by the Spray pyrolysis (SP) method on the glass substrate previously heated from 300 °C to 450 °C at 0.2 M. In order, to get a sufficiently transparent and conductive film, for to involve it as a window layer (TCO) in solar cells. The obtained results show that at 350 °C is suitable for producing the insulating and the transparent conductive layers of ZnO envisaged. The optical measurements show that transmittance reaches a maximum value of 70% in the visible region, which corresponds to the weak thickness value and refractive index. This corresponds to a maximum value for merit factor.

articleTitle: Improving PCE in Low Input Power Level RF Energy Harvesting using Sinc-like Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This paper presents a solution to improve the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of RF-to-dc conversion circuits especially when dealing with low RF power levels. It simply consists on the use of sinc-like Waveforms as a power optimized waveform (POW). The proposed approach is tested and validated in the case of a wide input power range rectifier using Software Defined Radio (SDR) to generate and transmit waveforms. For a PCE higher than 50%, the obtained results show an input power range of [-15 dBm to 19 dBm] in the case of sinc-like waveforms compared to [-10 dBm to 20 dBm] when using standard continuous waveforms (CW).

articleTitle: Subspace Coding for Error Control and Interference Mitigation in Routing Solutions with Cooperative Destination Nodes
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC) is a transmission scheme that opts for linear combinations of the transmitted packets at a subset of the intermediate nodes. This scheme is usually considered when Network Coding (NC) is desired over non-coherent networks. In order to integrate error correction in RLNC, subspace codes have been proposed. The codewords in those codes are unchanged under rank-preserving row operations, making them convenient for RLNC. In this paper, we investigate the use of those codes for the interference channel in a system model consisting of an array of SISO communication systems with cooperative destination nodes. This system model is deemed as a simplified model of a network with a routing based transmission scheme. Results have indicated that the use of subspace codes have allowed for better performance in terms of the decoding failure probability.

articleTitle: Experimental and Numerical Characterization of the PTFE Material in the X-Band Frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: This work aims to validate a characterisation method using a Poly-Tetra-Fluore-Ethylen. The method has been verified by three models: analytical model, numerical simulation and an experimental measurement. The analytical model is based on Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) method. The numerical simulation is performed using (Ansys HFSS) meaning a rectangular waveguide. The experimental measurement is done using a vector network analyzer (VNA) associated to a X-band waveguide system where the test samples were introduced by filling the cross-section of the waveguide. The result accuracy are enhanced by removing the phase ambiguity that introduced when using the measurement method, in both the experimental and the numerical methods. The results consist to obtain, respectively the complex permittivity and the complex permeability over the X-band frequency range considered [8 to 12 GHz].

articleTitle: Surface Potential Decay Evolution of Polypropylene Films Treated by Dielectric Barrier Discharge in Atmospheric Air
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: Dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) is a promising technique used to modify the surface properties of materials; it has been widely used in many domains such as ozone production, surface sterilization, and medical applications. In case of DBD surface functionalization, it requires a high AC voltage applied between two planar electrodes in addition to the presence of at least one dielectric barrier that separates the electrodes. The objective of this study is to assess how DBD treatment affects the evolution of surface potential decay following charging by negative corona discharge. The effects of treatment time and air length on the evolution of surface potential decay were the main purpose of this study. Water contact angle and surface potential decay measurements were used to evaluate surface characteristics of polypropylene (PP) before and after the DBD plasma modification. According to the experimental findings, plasma processing impacts surface wettability and surface potential decay. The decay rate values for short treatment duration are significantly different from those recorded for long treatment duration. The increase of surface potential decay rate demonstrates the introduction of polar groups by the plasma onto the PP surface, which causes a reduction in the water contact angle and speeds up the dissipation of surface charges.

articleTitle: Analytical magnetic field and eddy currents computation in a conductive rod wound by a cylindrical coil of finite length
publicationTitle: 2022 2nd International Conference on Advanced Electrical Engineering (ICAEE)
abstract: In this paper, we present an analytical model to calculate the magnetic field, the mutual inductance and eddy current in a long conductive rod wound by a cylindrical coil of finite length.
